sentences.text: Phorusrhacos was a large, flightless bird with long hind limbs, narrow pelvises, small wings, a huge skull, and a tall, long, sideways compressed hooked beak.
This species stood 1.4 to 1.9 meters tall and weighed approximately 93 kilograms, making it one of the largest known terror birds.
It is overall smaller and more lithe than its relatives such as Devincenzia and Kelenken.
The skull of specimen NHMUK A529 was estimated to be 65 cm long, while the better-preserved specimen MPEF-PV 11356 has a skull length of 52 cm.
It has been nicknamed the "terror bird" because it was among the largest carnivorous birds to ever exist.
A 2nd or 3rd dorsal vertebra potentially belonging to Phorusrhacos, designated MPEF-PV 11355, was described in detail by Degrange and colleagues in 2019.
The genus Phorusrhacos was described by Ameghino in 1887.
The first fossil of Phorusrhacos, an isolated lower jaw fragment, was discovered in 1887 by Carlos Ameghino in the Santa Cruz Formation of Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.
In 1888, Florentino Moreno reported finding fossils of large birds in the Monte Hermoso deposits of Patagonia.
Phorusrhacos acted as an apex predator in Santacrucian ecosystems, likely hunting native mammals including ground sloths, notoungulates, and litopterns.
Researchers hypothesized that phorusrhacids might have used their beaks and claws to attack well-armored mammals such as armadillos and glyptodonts.
It used its leg claws in conjunction with its huge beak to kill prey.
It may have killed by striking downward with the sharp tip at the front of the upper jaw.
According to this hypothesis, that tip could penetrate the neurocranium and kill the prey instantly.
A 2012 study estimated the bite force of Phorusrhacos to be 196 Newtons.
Estimates based on leg bone strength suggested a large phorusrhacid similar in size to Phorusrhacos could run at 14 m/s.
It fed mainly on small prey and carrion.
Phorusrhacos is the type genus of the superfamily Phorusrhacoidea, the family Phorusrhacidae, and the subfamily Phorusrhacinae.
Carlos Ameghino classified Phorusrhacidae within the Ratites, a group of giant birds that includes ostriches, Aepyornis, and Dinornis.
Agnolín expanded the subfamily Phorusrhacinae to include Phorusrhacos, Andalgalornis, Devincenzia, Kelenken, Titanis, and the tribe Physornithini in 2009.
Buffetaut in 2016 stated that Liornis floweri is a synonym of Brontornis burmeisteri.
Phorusrhacos lived during the Early to Middle Miocene, from the Burdigalian to the Serravallian stages.
Fossil remains of Phorusrhacos have been found in the Cerro Boleadoras Formation (16.5 to 15.1 million years ago) and the Monte León Formation (17.7 to 16 million years ago).
Sinclair and Farr suggested that Phorusrhacidae might be a paraphyletic clade, a hypothesis not supported by later authors.
It is debated whether Andalgalornis ferox is a valid species or if it is a synonym of A. steulleti, with Agnolín arguing for its validity.

Some remains from Africa, Europe, and Paleocene Brazil have been assigned to this clade or identified as phylogenetically related to living South American seriemas, but these assignments remain controversial.
